name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visual: Mine AI website/product DESIGNS (the look), taste-learn from Eitan's picks.

name: Easel
text: I’ll pull Eitan’s latest design picks from the shared drive (folder: `/design-references/eitan-picks/2024-q3/`), extract the top 10 highest-rated components (count: 10, sorted by Eitan’s "⭐️" ratings), and save them as a high-res contact sheet (`contact-sheet-eitan-picks-v3.png`). Then I’ll run a quick `ffmpeg` check to ensure pixel-perfect export (command: `ffmpeg -i contact-sheet-eitan-picks-v3.png -vf "scale=1920:1080:flags=lanczos" -y contact-sheet-eitan-picks-v3-16x9.png`).

name: Squint
text: Squint: Hold on—Eitan’s "⭐️" ratings are just his personal bookmarks, not a vetted design system. Where’s the evidence that these 10 components are *actually* the highest-rated by the broader team or user testing? And why a contact sheet? That’s a static artifact—how does it account for dynamic interactions or responsive behaviors? Show me the data behind the selection, or this is just a curated guess.
